findings.title: Lithuanian message replaced with Italian text
findings.body: File themes/src/main/resources-community/theme/base/account/messages/messages_lt.properties line 101 sets totpStep1 to Italian 'Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:' while the file is Lithuanian and surrounding keys are Lithuanian. The previous value was Lithuanian. Consequence is Lithuanian users will see Italian instructions. It should be Lithuanian text without HTML, not a copy of the Italian translation.

findings.title: Lithuanian login message replaced with Italian text
findings.body: File themes/src/main/resources-community/theme/base/login/messages/messages_lt.properties line 71 sets loginTotpStep1 to Italian 'Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:' while the file is Lithuanian and neighboring keys are Lithuanian. Consequence is Lithuanian login page shows Italian. It should be the Lithuanian translation without anchor tags.

findings.title: Simplified Chinese file contains Traditional Chinese
findings.body: File themes/src/main/resources-community/theme/base/account/messages/messages_zh_CN.properties line 112 sets totpStep1 to 'In your mobile...' using Traditional characters手机/應用程式/裝 while the file is zh_CN Simplified which elsewhere uses simplified 手机/应用 and surrounding lines are Simplified. Consequence is script inconsistency for Simplified Chinese users. It should use Simplified characters like 手机 and 应用程序.

findings.title: Missing English counterpart throws instead of reporting
findings.body: In VerifyMessageProperties.verifySafeHtml when the derived English file cannot be opened the code throws new RuntimeException. That aborts the whole verify() call, discarding any messages already collected and producing a stack trace instead of a normal verifier message. Consequence is a single community-only key or mis-mapped path fails the entire theme-verifier plugin with an exception and hides all other errors. It should record a message and continue.

findings.title: Dropped anchors pass silently and error lacks key/file
findings.body: Method santizeAnchors in VerifyMessageProperties iterates only over anchor tags found in the translation and strips exact matches. If the translation drops an anchor that exists in English, the loop runs zero times and passes with no error, so a lost link is never reported. When it does report, it adds only "Didn't find anchor tag ... in original string" with no key name and no file name, unlike the Illegal HTML message which includes both. Consequence is functional regressions are missed and failures that are reported are unactionable in logs covering hundreds of files.

findings.title: Semantically identical HTML flagged due to normalization
findings.body:
VerifyMessageProperties compares policy.sanitize(value) for exact string equality with the raw translation. The OWASP sanitizer normalizes markup such as
to
and to , so a safe translation using a different but equivalent spacing is reported as Illegal HTML. The PR itself proves this by having to rewrite dozens of webauthn-error and other messages only to add a space in
. Consequence is future translators writing valid
will fail verification. The verifier should normalize or allow equivalent serializations before comparing.

findings.title: No negative test for valid translations
findings.body:
All tests in VerifyMessagePropertiesTest assert hasItem for illegal cases such as duplicate keys, illegal tags, extra HTML, and changed anchors. There is no test asserting that a valid translation yields an empty message list, for example that noHtml_en, changedAnchor_en, or an English string with allowed /

/
passes. Consequence is false positives from sanitizer normalization or anchor stripping would not be caught by the test suite.
